summary: Quick bridgecall after last week's production spike where prefetch/prefix cache paths degraded and triggered fallbacks to cold KV reads. Discussed root cause hypothesis (race in prefetch worker + slightly different tokenization at edge), immediate mitigations, escrowed rollback plan, and security/compliance questions around cache flush and auditability.
topics: Root cause hypothesis: prefetch worker race & tokenization mismatch
Escrowed rollback runbook and who executes it
Security: audit logs, KMS, and data residency implications
Next steps: shadow deploy and benchmark
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Patel: All right, hey everyone thanks for jumping on. We know this is short notice, want to make sure we close the loop on the prefetch degradation incident.
[00:00:12] Omar Rahman: Yep thanks Maya. We had spike Friday where latency for the recommendation endpoint jumped from 120ms p95 to about 640ms and then redwood fallback kicked in, lots of cold kv reads, really burned tokens.
[00:00:30] Jenna Ortiz: And just to add — we saw a pattern where warm prefixes weren't being hit, but the same RPM earlier in the day was fine, so it's intermittent which makes it worse.
[00:00:44] Carlos Nguyen: Yeah, our preliminary archaeology suggests the prefetch worker hit a race when the kv-prefetch queue got backed up and then tokenization edge cases caused mismatched prefixes. So cache miss rate went up and continuous batching collapsed into per-request cold loads.
[00:01:05] Priya Desai: Can you explain the tokenization bit again? We use the open tokenizer that should be the same across stacks.
[00:01:12] Carlos Nguyen: Sure — in our repro the streaming token splitter at the edge trimmed different unicode sequences, there's a small normalization mismatch. In most traffic it's fine, but with certain user generated inputs we saw prefix keys not equal. It's subtle.
[00:01:30] Omar Rahman: That explains why the misses were bursty and tied to a subset of calls.
[00:01:36] Maya Patel: Ok, cool. So hypothesis: race in prefetch worker + tokenization mismatch = cache key divergence = high miss rate = fallback to cold KV = latency and cost spike.
[00:01:50] Jenna Ortiz: Sounds plausible. What mitigations can we do now? We need something safe, minimal blast radius.
[00:01:58] Carlos Nguyen: Immediate: 1) throttle prefetch concurrency for the hot-path so we avoid queue backpressure, 2) enable strict prefix normalization in the edge splitter (non breaking), 3) temporarily increase cache TTL for suspected keys. All three are low-risk and reversible.
[00:02:18] Priya Desai: Throttling might hurt throughput during high load; what's the tradeoff?
[00:02:25] Carlos Nguyen: Right — it'll increase per-request latency slightly but prevent the catastrophic collapse we saw. Think of it as load-shedding the prefetch workers. We'll tune in canary.
[00:02:36] Maya Patel: Also we talked about an escrowed rollback plan in case the patch causes regressions. That's the main reason for this call — to agree who can execute rollback and under what thresholds.
[00:02:47] Leo Grant: Security question: if you flush caches or change TTLs, what happens to audit logs? We need an auditable trail for any operations that touch customer data keys.
[00:02:58] Ruth Kim: Good call — we'll ensure all manual operations are executed via runbook steps that use the customer's KMS-backed key IDs and are logged into the audit stream. Carlos, can you outline the logging hooks?
[00:03:12] Carlos Nguyen: Yeah, every cache flush API call emits an event with key fingerprints but not raw payloads; those events are forwarded to the customer's audit log sink. For the rollback we'll centralize the steps in a runbook and attach the cloud/audit link.
[00:03:26] Omar Rahman: Ok we need that written and sent; legal will want it for our compliance review.
[00:03:31] Maya Patel: Agreed. Action here: Redwood to send rollback runbook that includes exact CLI/API commands and expected audit links.
[00:03:39] Jenna Ortiz: Another ask: can we get an exact list of the hosts and versions that were involved so we can cross-check with our observability?
[00:03:46] Carlos Nguyen: Yes we'll pull the host snapshot and the model runtime version; I'll include the nomination of which workers were on the suspect prefetch shard.
[00:03:55] Priya Desai: Do we have any reason to think this relates to quantization or is it purely prefetch logic?
[00:04:01] Carlos Nguyen: At this point it's prefetch/tokenization. Quantization doesn't change key generation. We will still run local regression with our quantized variants to be sure.
[00:04:12] Maya Patel: Cool. Let's talk about the canary and shadow deploy. Proposed plan: stage the patch into a small percentage of traffic (5%) for 24 hours behind a canary toggle, monitor p95 latency, cache hit ratio, and token cost delta. If metrics look good roll out to 50% then 100%.
[00:04:30] Jenna Ortiz: 5% seems fine, but we want to run the shadow (non-routed) replay as well to validate cache keys without impacting users.
[00:04:38] Ruth Kim: We'll coordinate a replay window; AstraScale to provide representative traffic snapshot.
[00:04:44] Maya Patel: Great. For the rollback escrow: we propose a two-person exec (Redwood SE + AstraScale SRE) to run the rollback runbook; rollback should be able to be completed within 12 minutes end-to-end.
[00:04:58] Leo Grant: Two-person execution is okay but we need a signed authorization flow and auditable confirmation.
[00:05:05] Maya Patel: Understood, we'll include auth steps in the runbook.
[00:05:09] Omar Rahman: What about capacity? If we make TTL longer as a mitigation, will that increase memory footprint on your side and potentially impact other customers?
[00:05:18] Carlos Nguyen: Good point — we prefer targeted TTL extension only for the affected prefixes (we can tag them). This avoids global footprint changes. If memory becomes a concern we fall back to throttling or temporary dedicated cache partitioning for AstraScale in dedicated capacity.
[00:05:34] Priya Desai: Dedicated partitioning — is that something we can get quickly?
[00:05:38] Maya Patel: We can stand up an isolated partition in Redwood Dedicated within the commit window, but that's a heavier operation and would be an enterprise action. For immediate mitigation we'll stick to targeted TTL + throttle + normalization.
[00:05:52] Jenna Ortiz: Sounds fine. Can we also get a short spreadsheet of token-cost delta from the incident? CFO will want the cost impact.
[00:05:59] Ruth Kim: We'll produce a short cost delta summary. Carlos, can engineering pull per-route token counts?
[00:06:06] Carlos Nguyen: Yes, we can slice by route and timeframe and export csv.
[00:06:10] Omar Rahman: Ok. On the compliance side, Leo will coordinate with Ruth and Maya to make sure the log retention and KMS usage meet our controls.
[00:06:18] Leo Grant: I'll send our retention requirements after the call.
[00:06:22] Maya Patel: Perfect. Any other concerns?
[00:06:25] Priya Desai: One more — do we have an end-to-end timeline for when the patch can be validated in production?
[00:06:30] Carlos Nguyen: If AstraScale can provide traffic snapshot by 2026-10-16 we'll aim to have a canary ready 2026-10-18 and run the 48-hour validation window starting then. That gives us space for coordination and the shadow replay.
[00:06:44] Jenna Ortiz: That timeline works.
[00:06:47] Maya Patel: Ok, I'll recap the explicit next steps at the top of the follow-up email.
[00:06:52] Ruth Kim: Quick note — we should also add a postmortem doc with timeline, impact, RCA and mitigations so customers and internal docs stay in sync.
[00:07:00] Maya Patel: Agreed — Ruth to produce the PM doc skeleton and we'll collaborate.
[00:07:05] Omar Rahman: One operational nit, make sure your cache-flush commands include a dry-run mode we can verify in staging.
[00:07:12] Carlos Nguyen: We'll include a dry-run that emits the audit events but doesn't mutate state; good suggestion.
[00:07:18] Maya Patel: Great. Let's list the explicit owners again quickly. Carlos will author rollback runbook and host snapshot, Ruth will coordinate pilot, Jenna will share traffic profile, Leo will confirm audit/retention.
[00:07:31] Priya Desai: And Redwood to provide cost delta csv and canary dashboards.
[00:07:36] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll send the follow-up within 24 hours.
[00:07:40] Omar Rahman: Appreciate it.
[00:07:42] Jenna Ortiz: Thanks all.
[00:07:45] [meeting ends]
